materials.content:
A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, or audit behavior. Preserve the ordinary
streaming path and subsequent uses. The queue-record format is outside this fix.

# Transfer retry panel

This frontend workspace selects files, starts transfers, and shows queued status.
Run with Node v16.20.2; there are no dependencies. `src/workspace.js` exports
`createTransferWorkspace({ transport, onCancel, record, showQueued })`. Each
workspace has independent visit and attempt counters. A `select(file)` call
opens a new visit, including when the exact same file object is selected again.
`retry()` accepts one retry for the current visit; `hide()` closes its panel;
`dispose()` ends the workspace. `snapshot()` exposes current ownership.

Retry already cancels the previous transfer before enqueueing an accepted retry. Preserve that behavior during progress maintenance.
An accepted retry always belongs to the file and visit present at entry, creates
exactly one new attempt, and remains in the queue record even if cancellation
causes navigation. Attempt IDs increase once per enqueued command within each
workspace; navigation must not retarget an accepted retry to the newly selected
file or drop its command. Queueing and recording are synchronous.

Cancellation uses a native `AbortController`: `abort()` synchronously calls the
host's `onCancel` observer before returning. That observer may select another
file, hide the panel, or hide and reopen the identical file object. New selection
immediately starts its own transfer. The newer visit must retain its view and
handle when the older retry resumes. Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file.
Normal retries in a current visit still issue one queued notice each.

The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record. There must be no remaining active
transfer from that old visit. The new visit remains able to retry and hide;
hiding cancels its owned handle and repeated cancellation is idempotent.
Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership. A hidden panel
accepts no retry. Workspace disposal cancels every remaining transfer and is
idempotent. Disposing one workspace cannot affect another.

`transport({file, attemptId, signal})` starts a pending physical transfer and
observes the native signal. `record` and `showQueued` are passive synchronous
sinks. Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;
`kind` is `select` or `retry`. Adding `byteCount` from `file.size` is an adjacent
record-format extension requiring separate authorization. Notices remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}`. Preserve these public interfaces.

## Transfer progress

A file may supply a shared `progressFeed` with a native EventTarget `target`,
`start()`, and `decode(packet)`. Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target.
Events are named `progress` and their detail is decoded to `{seq, loaded}`.
Decoding may return a value or a Promise. The same file and source can be reused
by multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription.

The workspace accepts `recordProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})` and
`showProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})`. The former is a passive retained audit
sink. Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes. A retired visit
accepts no new progress events. Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live. `showProgress` may synchronously select or hide through
the workspace, and normal current progress must remain visible. Progress does
not change queue records, native transfer cancellation, or accepted retry policy.
Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained. Preserve these adapter interfaces.

obligations.statement: Cancel the previous transfer before enqueueing an accepted retry.
obligations.event_relation: Previous native abort precedes retry enqueue.
obligations.failure_if_violated: Old and retry transfers remain active together.

obligations.statement: An accepted retry retains its entry file and visit, queues once and records once even after navigation.
obligations.failure_if_violated: Retry is dropped, duplicated, or retargeted.
required_concepts: command acceptance differs from view ownership

obligations.statement: A retired visit emits no queued notice, including after identical-file reopening; current retries remain live.
obligations.event_relation: Visit retirement precedes exclusion of subsequent notices.
obligations.failure_if_violated: Old queued status appears in the newer visit or hidden panel.
required_concepts: visit identity differs from file identity

obligations.statement: Newer navigation keeps its transfer owner and remains usable for retry and hide; no retired transfer stays active.
obligations.event_relation: Abort callback navigation precedes older retry continuation.
obligations.failure_if_violated: The outer retry steals the newer handle or leaves an abandoned transfer.
required_concepts: canceling a retained retired command cannot cancel a newer owner

obligations.statement: Cancellation and disposal are idempotent, hidden retry is a no-op, and independent workspaces stay independent.
obligations.event_relation: Workspace retirement prevents new commands only in that workspace.
obligations.failure_if_violated: Repeated callbacks or shared counters revoke unrelated work.

obligations.statement: Queue records retain their existing fields unless byteCount is explicitly granted.
obligations.failure_if_violated: Unrequested schema expansion or omitted authorized byteCount.
required_concepts: scope and temporal correctness are distinct

obligations.statement: A retired visit accepts no new progress; accepted decoding still records history, while visible progress requires a current visit.
obligations.event_relation: Admission precedes decoding; retirement ends new admission, not accepted history work.
obligations.failure_if_violated: Retired listeners accept new frames or accepted decode history is lost.

materials.content: Restore the initial progress update from a warm progress source. The source may emit cached progress synchronously when a subscription starts, but the current watcher starts it before attaching the listener. Accepted events must be decoded and audited once, even if decoding completes after the visit closes; visible progress belongs only to the current visit. Preserve later streaming events, reuse of the source across visits, retry and cancellation behavior, navigation ownership, cleanup, and the existing queue-record format.

feedback.causal_status: No cause independently verified; see evidence ledger for separately authored source reasoning.

evidence.statement: Restore the initial warm-source update, preserving ordinary streaming and existing transfer/retry/navigation/cleanup/audit behavior; record-format extension is outside scope.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

anchors.quote:
A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, or audit behavior. Preserve the ordinary
streaming path and subsequent uses. The queue-record format is outside this fix.

evidence.statement: Starting the shared progress source can emit synchronously; decoding can settle synchronously or later and the same source can be reused across visits.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

anchors.quote:
A file may supply a shared `progressFeed` with a native EventTarget `target`,
`start()`, and `decode(packet)`. Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target.
Events are named `progress` and their detail is decoded to `{seq, loaded}`.
Decoding may return a value or a Promise. The same file and source can be reused
by multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription.

evidence.statement: Each admitted event must retain exactly one audit at decode completion even after departure; retired visits admit no new events; visible updates stop on closing/replacement; callbacks may reenter.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

anchors.quote:
The workspace accepts `recordProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})` and
`showProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})`. The former is a passive retained audit
sink. Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes. A retired visit
accepts no new progress events. Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live. `showProgress` may synchronously select or hide through
the workspace, and normal current progress must remain visible. Progress does
not change queue records, native transfer cancellation, or accepted retry policy.
Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained. Preserve these adapter interfaces.

evidence.statement: An accepted retry is bound at entry, cancellation precedes enqueue, exactly one retained command survives reentrant navigation.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

anchors.quote:
Retry already cancels the previous transfer before enqueueing an accepted retry. Preserve that behavior during progress maintenance.
An accepted retry always belongs to the file and visit present at entry, creates
exactly one new attempt, and remains in the queue record even if cancellation
causes navigation. Attempt IDs increase once per enqueued command within each
workspace; navigation must not retarget an accepted retry to the newly selected
file or drop its command. Queueing and recording are synchronous.

evidence.statement: Native abort callbacks run synchronously and may navigate or reopen identical data; newer visit retains ownership. Retained retry and cleanup obligations remain.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

anchors.quote:
Cancellation uses a native `AbortController`: `abort()` synchronously calls the
host's `onCancel` observer before returning. That observer may select another
file, hide the panel, or hide and reopen the identical file object. New selection
immediately starts its own transfer. The newer visit must retain its view and
handle when the older retry resumes. Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file.
Normal retries in a current visit still issue one queued notice each.

The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record. There must be no remaining active
transfer from that old visit. The new visit remains able to retry and hide;
hiding cancels its owned handle and repeated cancellation is idempotent.
Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership. A hidden panel
accepts no retry. Workspace disposal cancels every remaining transfer and is
idempotent. Disposing one workspace cannot affect another.

evidence.statement: Keep public sink and queue interfaces; adjacent record extension needs separate authorization.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

anchors.quote:
`transport({file, attemptId, signal})` starts a pending physical transfer and
observes the native signal. `record` and `showQueued` are passive synchronous
sinks. Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;
`kind` is `select` or `retry`. Adding `byteCount` from `file.size` is an adjacent
record-format extension requiring separate authorization. Notices remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}`. Preserve these public interfaces.

evidence.statement: Current listener delivers to record and view after decode; current source calls source start before adding its listener. This ordering is a current fact, not intended preservation.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

evidence.statement: The audit callback captures entry file/attempt, while visible delivery checks current visit identity.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

evidence.statement: Transfer owns a controller and a deferred cleanup callback; its abort invokes cleanup and synchronous cancellation observer. The returned resource remains attempt-local.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

evidence.statement: Selection publishes an identity before enqueue, then checks whether it is still current before assigning the resulting handle; hide invalidates before releasing.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

evidence.statement: Retry captures current visit, cancels prior handle and enqueues for the captured visit; active view identity gates publication.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

evidence.statement: Preservation applies to documented accepted audit/retry histories and visit-owned display/resource semantics; it does not authorize retaining the reported missing-initial-update defect.
evidence.author: execution_agent_source_review

constraints.statement: Restore supported initial and subsequent event delivery without imposing an unevidenced implementation.
Retain exactly-once accepted audit through later decode, but stop retired admission and visible effects according to documented policies.
Keep newer visit ownership, entry-bound retry/record and attempt cancellation semantics under synchronous reentry and late handles.
Keep shared-source reuse, independent owners and existing interfaces; do not add record-format extensions.

mechanism_predicates.shared_lifetime: 修复对象的共享状态或工作可超出单个消费者寿命
mechanism_predicates.observer_lifetime: 多个消费者通过独立订阅/观察者身份共享同一工作
mechanism_predicates.attempt_resource: 每次执行尝试有独立取消资源或完成身份
mechanism_predicates.lazy_consumption: 读取取消能力会同步记录实际消费，且其归属可由当前证据核查
mechanism_predicates.async_resume: 暂停/重试工作可通过异步续行恢复
mechanism_predicates.deferred_batch: 修复对象将连续输入合并为可挂起的延迟工作
mechanism_predicates.boundary_persistence: 当前文档规定离开/提交边界返回前须结算已接纳的持久化义务
mechanism_predicates.entry_snapshot: 接纳的操作绑定入口选择/数据，后续重入不应改写其既成义务
mechanism_predicates.inline_reentry: 结算/通知会同步调用可重入导航/编辑的回调
mechanism_predicates.effect_lifetimes: 持久结果和当前界面反馈具有可区分的归属与有效期
mechanism_predicates.different_ownership_policy: 当前任务明确要求与共享状态及尝试分离相矛盾的所有权政策
mechanism_predicates.discard_boundary_policy: 当前任务明确允许丢弃目标的已接纳持久义务而非结算
mechanism_predicates.no_lazy_shared_mechanism: 当前证据明确表明修复对象没有共享状态与惰性消费机制
